Yesterday, Mrs Perkins presented complaining of food poisoning symptoms, including bilious vomiting
and mild abdominal pain for which fluids, analgesia and metoclopramide were given. Today, her

and has experienced constipation for four days.

Deleted: e

On examination, Mrs Perkins’s abdomen was tender and bloated for which and no bowel sounds could
be heard. Although her blood pressure was low, her pulse rate was high. Her abdomen was tympanic on
palpation and the skin was clammy. Despite the fact that her potassium, magnesium and creatinine
were low, her urea was high. An abdominal x-ray revealed a coffee bean shape mass which indicate a
possible stricture. Due to a diagnosis of a large bowel obstruction, a nasogastric decompression was
conducted, and intravenous fluids and analgesia were commenced. Kindly note, she has Chron’s disease,
had childhood volvulus and has a positive family history of colon cancer.
